claims.claim: **Hypocalcaemia = total calcium under 2.2 mmol/L or ionised calcium under 1 mmol/L**; symptoms typically start below a total of 1.8 mmol/L. Not for neonates under 1 month.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severity by total calcium:** mild under 2.2 (asymptomatic) · moderate under 1.8 (paraesthesia, cramps, tetany) · severe under 1.6 (arrhythmia, stridor, apnoea, confusion, seizures). ⚠️ **Any severe feature = treat as severe whatever the level.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Commonest causes: vitamin D deficiency and PTH deficiency.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Collect before replacing if possible:** corrected and ionised calcium, UEC, magnesium, phosphate, 25-hydroxy vitamin D, PTH, and an **ECG for QTc prolongation or arrhythmia.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Replace calcium if corrected calcium is under 2.0 mmol/L or ionised under 1.0 mmol/L, or there are symptoms, signs or ECG changes.** Moderate–severe hypocalcaemia needs ECG monitoring and IV access.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Correct magnesium and potassium too** — if hypomagnesaemia is left untreated, hypocalcaemia may not respond to treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral/enteral is preferred, given with food.** Consider IV for severe acute hypocalcaemia or ECG changes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute oral dose (elemental calcium):** 1 month–12 years **10–20 mg/kg orally qid**, increasing as needed (to a maximum of 120–200 mg/kg/day); ages 12–18 years **1–2 g daily in 3 or 4 divided doses.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also give calcitriol daily, 0.015 microg/kg (max 0.25 microg)**; it increases calcium absorption within 1–2 days. Monitor calcium and phosphate every few days until they are stable, and every 1–2 weeks after that.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintenance / recommended daily elemental calcium:** 1–3 years 500 mg · 4–8 years 700 mg · 9–11 years 1000 mg · 12–18 years 1300 mg orally; monitor 6-monthly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tablets:** Cal-500 / Cal-Sup = 500 mg elemental calcium (1250 mg carbonate); Cal-600 = 600 mg (1500 mg carbonate). Check other products' strengths carefully.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Both calcium chloride and gluconate are vesicants** — extravasation risks necrosis; **gluconate is preferred without central access.** ⚠️ **Rapid administration can cause hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmia and cardiac arrest.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Target a safe range: corrected calcium over 1.8 or ionised over 1.0.** Switch to oral as soon as the child is stable. Discuss with ICU/retrieval if an IV infusion is needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Calcium gluconate (2.2 mmol per 10 mL), ages 1 month–18 years:** large vein IV or IO, **0.07–0.14 mmol/kg given over 10–60 minutes (max 4.4 mmol)**, repeated every 4–6 hours if needed until asymptomatic; may follow with an infusion of 0.44–1.76 mmol/kg/day.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Calcium chloride 10%, 1 month–18 years:** large vein IV or IO, **0.07–0.14 mmol/kg over at least 6 minutes (max 6.8 mmol)**; an infusion of 0.5–1 mmol/kg/day may follow. Initially, check calcium every 6–8 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dilution:** calcium gluconate (0.22 mmol/mL) to 0.11 mmol/mL or weaker; calcium chloride (0.68 mmol/mL) to 0.14 mmol/mL or weaker.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer if** ionised calcium under 1.0 or corrected under 1.8, symptomatic, significant ECG changes (prolonged QT, arrhythmia), neonate, or complex medical condition. Involve endocrinology if the suspected cause is something other than vitamin D deficiency.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when asymptomatic with a stable corrected calcium over 1.8 mmol/L** and a plan for monitoring and follow-up of the cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypocalcaemia' (Last updated July 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypocalcaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
